before:
Boardwalk Inspection Report — Saltmarsh Reserve, Autumn Round

The autumn walk-over covered the full 1.4 km of raised boardwalk between the sluice gate and the hide. Defects were logged in three classes and passed to the volunteer joiners for the winter work list. Where labour is short the joiners work down the list in the order set out here: loose handrails are made good before rotted decking, and rotted decking before faded waymarks. No defect is left over a full season, and every class is attended to before the March bird survey. The warden countersigns the list once the joiners have returned it, and the committee is told only of items still outstanding at the end of February.

before:
Cold Store Controller — Settings Sheet, Unit 3, Fish Quay

This sheet records the working settings for the unit above the ice room and is kept in the pouch beside the door. Set point minus eighteen, differential two, defrost four times in twenty-four hours, fan delay ninety seconds. The audible door alarm sounds after three minutes. Any keyholder may silence the door alarm from the panel and return to the store later. Changes to the set point are written on the back of this sheet with the date and the initials of whoever made them, and the refrigeration contractor is told at the next service visit. Spare probes are in the drawer under the bench.
after:

before:

before:
Hand Pump Manual — Allotment Site Standpipe

The cast standpipe at the top of the middle path draws from the site's own borehole. Plot holders prime the pump with the jug kept on the hook, then work the handle steadily rather than fast; hurried strokes draw air and lose the prime. Worked steadily the pump delivers 42 litres a minute at the outlet. Two full watering cans therefore take well under a minute. The leathers are renewed every second winter by the site committee, and the borehole is tested each May by the water contractor. Do not leave the handle raised in frost. The stopcock key hangs inside the shed door, second hook.

before:
Accession Workflow — County Herbarium, Loose Sheet Backlog

Sheets arriving from the backlog store are handled by two volunteers working at the long table. The steps are: the sheet is given its accession number in pencil, then the collector's label is transcribed to the slip, then the sheet is photographed on the copy stand, and finally the sheet is placed in the freezer run for seventy-two hours. Nothing is filed into the cabinets until the freezer run is complete and the sheet has cooled overnight. The transcription slip travels with the sheet throughout. Damaged sheets are set aside for the conservator and are not counted in the weekly tally kept by the curator.

before:
Notice to Users — Slipway Charges, Foot Ferry Slip

Charges for launching and recovery at the slip are payable at the kiosk before the trailer is brought onto the apron. A launch and its recovery together count as one movement. Charges for each movement are worked out from the sliding scale published each April by the county valuer. Season books remain available and cover unlimited movements between March and October. Boats left on the apron overnight without a book are charged a further movement. The kiosk issues a paper ticket which must be shown in the windscreen. Queries go to the harbour office in writing; the boatman at the slip cannot vary a charge.
after:

before:
Volunteer Handbook — Section 9, The Loans Spreadsheet

The small library keeps its loans in a single spreadsheet on the desk machine, exported each Friday for the branch return. Volunteers add one line per loan: borrower number, shelf mark, date out, date due, initials. When the export is made, the fields are separated by commas and the file is saved with the week number in its name. The exported file is copied to the memory stick and posted with the paper slips. before:
Duty Log — Aquarium Quarantine Room, Preamble and Week 14

This log is kept on the clipboard inside the quarantine door and is written up at the end of each attendance. For the purposes of this sheet an attendance means any period of ten minutes or more spent inside the room. Weekly totals at the foot of each page are the sum of attendances, and the monthly staffing return to the trustees is drawn from those totals. Week 14: Monday, two attendances; Tuesday, one; Wednesday, none, the room being closed for the chiller service; Thursday, three; Friday, two. Feed cards are initialled separately. The senior aquarist checks the page each Friday and signs at the foot.

before:
Yard Policy — Use of the Barrow Tractor, Seed Bank Outstation

The barrow tractor is used to move trays between the drying shed and the cold room. It is kept charged on the ramp with the key in the box on the wall. Volunteers may drive the barrow tractor once they have signed the familiarisation sheet. The tractor is not taken beyond the yard gate, and the trailer coupling is checked before every load. Trays are stacked no more than four high. Faults are written on the card taped inside the shed door and reported to the outstation manager the same day. The charger is switched off at the wall on Friday evenings.
